n: Asaph, one of David’s chief musicians, pictures a great courtroom. God speaks and summons the whole earth, from east to west, as witnesses.

f.w: The mighty God, even the LORD
f.g: Three divine names in Hebrew: El, Elohim, YHWH — a majestic opening.

f.w: from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof

n: God shines out from Zion, the most beautiful place, like the sun rising.

f.w: the perfection of beauty
God hath shined

n: God comes with fire and storm, as he did at Sinai. He will not stay silent any longer.

f.w: a fire shall devour before him

n: He calls heaven and earth as witnesses in his case against his own people.

f.w: He shall call to the heavens from above

n: “Gather my faithful ones” — those who entered into covenant with God through sacrifice. Latter-day Saints see in this gathering a theme of the last days.

f.w: Gather my saints together unto me
made a covenant with me by sacrifice

n: Heaven proclaims that God is just — he is the judge himself.
The case begins. God addresses Israel personally: I am your God, and I am testifying against you.

f.w: testify against thee

n: The problem isn’t that they failed to offer sacrifices — they offered them constantly.

f.w: reprove

n: God doesn’t need any of their bulls or goats.
Every animal already belongs to him — even the cattle grazing on a thousand hills.

f.w: the cattle upon a thousand hills

n: He knows every bird and wild creature. Nothing in creation is outside his ownership.
Even if God were hungry — which he is not — he wouldn’t need to ask them. The whole world is his.

f.w: the world is mine, and the fulness thereof

n: A gently ironic question: do I eat meat and drink blood? Sacrifice was never meant to feed God.
What God really wants is a thankful heart and faithfulness to the promises they’ve made.

f.w: Offer unto God thanksgiving
pay thy vows
f.g: Keep the promises you made to God.

n: And he wants them to call on him in trouble. He will rescue them, and they will give him glory. Relationship matters more than ritual.

f.w: call upon me in the day of trouble

n: Now God turns to the wicked: what right do you have to recite my laws and talk about my covenant?

f.w: take my covenant in thy mouth

n: You hate correction and toss my words behind your back.

f.w: castest my words behind thee
f.g: Treat them as worthless, throw them away.

n: When you see a thief, you join him; you keep company with adulterers. These echo the Ten Commandments.

f.w: thief

n: Your mouth is full of evil and your tongue weaves lies.

f.w: frameth

n: You sit around slandering your own brother — your mother’s son.
God was silent, and they assumed he was like them — indifferent to sin. Now he will lay out the evidence before their eyes.

f.w: thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself

n: A solemn warning to those who forget God: consider this now, before judgment comes and no one can save you.

f.w: ye that forget God

n: The final word: anyone who offers thanks honors God, and anyone who walks the right path will see God’s salvation.

f.w: ordereth his conversation aright
f.g: Sets his way of life in order; “conversation” means conduct.
